h1: What do AI security agents find that SAST does not, and what do they miss that SAST catches?
subtitle: An attacker-reachable recall study of deterministic SAST and AI security agents
lede: We ran nine productized security configurations once each, blind, on 20 open-source web applications. For the seven endpoint-aware configurations, a finding counts only when it locates the attacker-controlled source and the dangerous sink of a curated vulnerability, each within two lines; DeepSec is scored separately.

headline_evidence.h2: Close at the top. Different ground covered.
headline_evidence.chart: figure 1 (all seven endpoint-aware configurations; DeepSec in its own panel)
callouts: Snyk Code 82.4% (89 of 108) and Claude Code /security-review with Opus 5 xhigh 79.3% (85 of 108): they disagree on 28 vulnerabilities, 16 to 12, too few to tell them apart.
Together they match 101 of 108, the same as all seven endpoint-aware configurations combined: a ceiling across configurations, not one tool's result.
DeepSec is scored with localized recall, a different evidence requirement, and is shown separately.
headline_evidence.for_appsec: In this study neither engine was sufficient alone. A vulnerability class an engine does not report is a real miss here, because every reference vulnerability is attacker-reachable.
headline_evidence.dataset_line: Dataset 2.0.0 · Snyk VulnBench 2.0 · 108 reference vulnerabilities · one run per configuration and application · Source: published 2.0 paper

findings_intro.kicker: What the results mean in practice
findings_intro.h2: An AI security engine is a model inside a harness.
findings_intro.body: Deterministic SAST and AI review covered different ground; what an AI engine reported depended on its harness as much as on its model; and coverage and cost were only loosely related.

principles.body: VulnBench is a versioned research initiative, not a universal leaderboard. Every release defines what it measured and what it did not prove.

items.title: Independent reference sets
items.text: 2.0 scores against curated, attacker-reachable vulnerabilities, not against any tool's findings.

items.title: Strict, stated scoring
items.text: A finding counts only when it locates the curated vulnerability's endpoints; alternative scoring rules are reported, not hidden.

items.title: Same rules for every system
items.text: Every configuration is named in full and scored by the same rule; DeepSec's different metric is never ranked with the others.

items.title: Reproducible data
items.text: The harness, reference sets and every run are public and checksummed.

items.title: Explicit limitations
items.text: Agreement is never relabeled as accuracy, and findings outside the reference set are never called false.

release_history_note: Releases measure different things. JS 1.0 measured repeatability and agreement with Snyk Code; 2.0 measures attacker-reachable recall against an independent reference set.
